  <div class="attributed-text-segment-list__container relative mt-1 mb-1.5 babybear:mt-0 babybear:mb-0.5">
    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="feed-reshare-content__commentary">The Pacific Apiculture Value Chain Initiative is a sectoral workstream aimed at supporting holistic interventions across the enabling environment for the apiculture value chain. 

This initiative sits under the deepening Forum Markets priority area of the Pacific Aid-for-Trade Strategy 2026-2030 and is linked to the Resource and Economic Development thematic area of the 2050 Strategy of the Blue Pacific Continent.  

The first phase of the Pacific Apiculture Value Chain Initiative is being delivered through the Pacific Beekeeping Enabling Environment  (BEE) Project by the Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat and with the support of AsureQuality. 

The current phase will be implemented across seven Forum Island Countries including Niue, Fiji, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga and Vanuatu.

The first official in-country mission for the Pacific BEE Project was successfully concluded in Niue last week. Our team toured <a class="link" href="https://www.linkedin.com/signup/cold-join?session_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Ffeed%2Fhashtag%2Ftherock&trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card_reshare-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card_reshare-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>#TheRock</a> to conduct hive inspections, collect bee samples for diagnostic testing, and observe current apiary practices alongside local beekeepers. 

The team also reconnected with government counterparts in Alofi to gather information, discuss current systems, and progress key project milestones.
This regional initiative supported by the Standards and Trade Development Facility (STDF) and the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT).

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary"><a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/fonterra?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Fonterra</a>’s recent invitation for applications from South Island organic farmers has sparked renewed interest in organic conversion. From our conversations at Southern Field Days last week, we know farmers are keen to explore the shift to organic production and are looking for answers. Some of the common queries relate to animal health, boundary management, pest and weed control and the challenges of running organic and conventional herds together. This is where AsureQuality’s expert team can help. 

In our recent webinar, hosted alongside Fonterra, we addressed these topics, and explained how AsureQuality supports dairy farmers through the organic conversion process, with insights from a certified organic farmer, along with practical guidance on what to expect during conversion.

We also extend our thanks to Southern Organic Group and Fonterra for including us on their sites and for the opportunity to engage with farmers face to face. 🤝
